summary: Fixed publisher-side NOTIFY gaps with bounded queued first delivery and retryable remote resync. Before-fix regression failed as expected; final 19 synthetic tests and server typecheck pass.
limitations: Synthetic fake-transport tests establish application recovery behavior; no live PostgreSQL, browser, full suite, build, deployed server, git action or external database was used.

Recovery state is intentionally in memory. A publisher process that dies before successfully notifying a pending gap cannot guarantee delivery after its restart; durable revision tracking/outbox remains outside this bounded fix.
One already-started pool query can settle (and may deliver its notification) after close. The database API has no query cancellation primitive; its eventual completion cannot requeue work.

A pool query that never settles prevents further transport attempts on this relay; payload retention stays bounded. Recovery assumes the transport eventually completes or rejects and the process remains running.

Receiving instances must support the new resync control envelope; older deployed versions do not understand it. Coordinate rollout or use the existing browser reconnect invalidation during a mixed-version interval.
Remote control resync invalidates all connected workspaces on that schema rather than retaining an unbounded set of affected workspace IDs. No load/capacity target is asserted.
